content.content:
---
name: neurico-host-local-llm-fallback
description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent; GPUs are shared/contended; vLLM recipe, cached models, and pitfalls (pkill self-kill, cudnn clash, prompt_logprobs OOM)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e7324b18-29e9-4db0-ae5a-a9f0cd196a49
  modified: 2026-10-16T18:23:14.513Z
---

Observed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16 in neurico research workspaces on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env (`~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` has it commented out). Resource-finder stage may be skipped (no papers/, datasets/, code/).
- Local models + datasets cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (HF_HOME=/data/transformers): Qwen2.5-{0.5,1.5,3,7,14}B-Instruct safetensors, Qwen3/3.5 family, Llama-3.1-8B, GGUFs; datasets incl. glue(sst2 only), stanfordnlp/sst2, samsum, ag_news, boolq, mmlu. huggingface.co is reachable for extra downloads (curl resolve/main URLs).
- 2026-10-16: 4x RTX A6000 (48GB) present but shared — other users' jobs held ~42GB on 3 GPUs and intermittently grabbed the 4th. Approach that worked: vLLM 0.31 (`uv add "vllm>=0.10"`; unpinned `uv add vllm` resolved an ancient 0.4 build), small `gpu_memory_utilization` (~0.11 ≈ 5GB) for ≤1.5B models on the leftover slices, plus a bash wrapper that polls `nvidia-smi` free memory and retries launch. vLLM checks free mem ≥ util×total at startup.
- 2026-10-14 (no GPU then): llama.cpp multi-server CPU fallback worked; `transformers` CPU generation much slower.
- Pitfalls: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash call whose text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (find PIDs, kill by PID separately). Leftover `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 8.x from a failed install breaks flashinfer ("Found 2 libcudnn.so.x") — `uv pip uninstall nvidia-cudnn-cu12`. vLLM `prompt_logprobs` materialises full-vocab logits → OOM on small slices; cap `max_num_batched_tokens` (~1024). Don't edit a bash script while a running loop is executing it.
- Label-restricted log-probs in vLLM: `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` + `allowed_token_ids=label_ids` returns log-softmax renormalised over the labels.

Update 2026-10-16 (inter-model-agreement workspace): 4×A6000 present but shared — other neurico sessions keep each GPU at ~6–10 GB free, fluctuating second to second. What worked:
- `uv venv --python 3.12` (default 3.14 breaks vLLM); pyproject needs `requires-python="==3.12.*"` and `[tool.uv] package=false`.
- vLLM 0.31: no bitsandbytes; set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (JIT build fails); `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Use pre-quantized 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ checkpoints (~5.5 GB for 8B): Qwen/*-AWQ, hugging-quants Llama-3.1/gemma-2 AWQ-INT4, tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, solidrust Mistral AWQ, kaitchup Olmo-3/Phi-3 GPTQ.
- Cap gpu_memory_utilization to ~12.5 GB and retry on startup OOM via a scheduler loop; max_model_len 2560, max_num_seqs 64.
- Gated models in /data/transformers/hub (meta-llama Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, google/gemma-7b-it) have weights but no config/tokenizer → unusable; unsloth mirror of Llama-3.1 is complete. Disk /data is ~100% full.

Update 2026-10-16 (few-shot-ordering workspace, 2nd session): a "Begin research execution" prompt can land on a workspace where a prior session already finished most work (REPORT.md exists, background jobs killed at session end). Check logs/*.status and REPORT first and resume only the interrupted pieces rather than restarting. Monitor `tail -n0 -F` on status files missed an append; poll status files directly instead. Qwen2.5-14B bf16 (~30 GB) won't fit when GPUs have ≤23 GB free.

Update 2026-10-16 (system_prompt_residual_effects workspace): the neurico runner can kill a session at its 6h limit (return_code 143) and relaunch with the same prompt while detached background jobs (e.g. `run_all.sh`) keep running. On start, check for existing planning.md/REPORT.md, `*_PLACEHOLDER` markers, `.neurico/pipeline_*.json`, `*.partial` checkpoints and live PIDs before redoing anything; usually you only need to wait for the jobs and re-run the scoring/analysis.

idea:
  title: "Quantization Failure Modes: Task-Specific Accuracy Cliffs in Weight-Reduced Language Models"
  description: >
    Post-training quantization (INT8, INT4, GPTQ, AWQ) is widely used to
    reduce model size, but accuracy degradation is not uniform across tasks.
    Some tasks tolerate aggressive quantization while others hit sharp
    accuracy cliffs. This study maps the task-specific failure landscape
    of quantization across reasoning, factual recall, and generation tasks.

    We quantize 3 model families (Qwen-2.5, Llama-3, Phi-3) at 4 precision
    levels (FP16, INT8, INT4, 2-bit) and evaluate on 6 task types:
    (1) arithmetic reasoning, (2) factual QA, (3) code generation,
    (4) reading comprehension, (5) creative writing, and (6) instruction
    following. For each combination we measure accuracy, output perplexity,
    and token-level KL divergence from the FP16 baseline. We identify
    "cliff tasks" where accuracy drops by more than 15% between adjacent
    precision levels.

    Use locally runnable models via Ollama. Write a computational paper
    under 3000 words with 2-3 figures.
  hypothesis: >
    Arithmetic reasoning and factual QA are the most quantization-sensitive
    tasks, showing cliff behavior between INT8 and INT4 (>15% accuracy drop).
    Creative writing and reading comprehension are robust down to INT4.
    Smaller models within a family show cliffs at higher precision than
    larger models. KL divergence predicts cliff onset (threshold ~0.3 nats)
    before accuracy visibly degrades.
  domain: artificial_intelligence
  references:
    - "Dettmers et al. (2022) GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-Trained Transformers"
    - "Lin et al. (2024) AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration"

"""Build the fixed evaluation suite (6 task types) and save it to datasets/suite.jsonl.

Each item: {task, id, messages (chat), max_tokens, gold (task-specific)}.
Sampling is seeded (42) so the suite is reproducible.
"""
import json
import random
from pathlib import Path

from datasets import load_dataset

SEED = 42
N = {"arith": 250, "factqa": 400, "reading": 400, "code": 164, "instr": 300, "creative": 100}
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "datasets"


def sample(ds, n, seed=SEED):
    idx = list(range(len(ds)))
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(idx)
    return [ds[i] for i in idx[:n]]


def main():
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    items = []

    # (1) Arithmetic reasoning: GSM8K test, zero-shot chain of thought.
    gsm = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="test")
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(gsm, N["arith"])):
        gold = ex["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip().replace(",", "")
        items.append(dict(task="arith", id=f"gsm{i}", max_tokens=512, gold=gold, messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            ex["question"] + "\n\nSolve the problem step by step. End your response with the line "
            "'The answer is N' where N is the final number."}]))

    # (2) Factual QA: TriviaQA (closed book), short answer, alias match.
    tqa = load_dataset("mandarjoshi/trivia_qa", "rc.nocontext", split="validation")
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(tqa, N["factqa"])):
        aliases = sorted(set(ex["answer"]["normalized_aliases"] + [ex["answer"]["normalized_value"]]))
        items.append(dict(task="factqa", id=f"tqa{i}", max_tokens=32, gold=aliases, messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Answer the trivia question with only the answer (a few words), no explanation.\n\nQuestion: "
            + ex["question"] + "\nAnswer:"}]))

    # (3) Reading comprehension: SQuAD v1.1 validation, extractive span.
    sq = load_dataset("rajpurkar/squad", split="validation")
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(sq, N["reading"])):
        items.append(dict(task="reading", id=f"squad{i}", max_tokens=32, gold=ex["answers"]["text"], messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Read the passage and answer the question with a short span copied from the passage. "
            "Reply with only the answer.\n\nPassage: " + ex["context"] + "\n\nQuestion: " + ex["question"] + "\nAnswer:"}]))

    # (4) Code generation: HumanEval (all 164), executed with unit tests.
    he = load_dataset("openai/openai_humaneval", split="test")
    for ex in he:
        items.append(dict(task="code", id=ex["task_id"], max_tokens=512,
                          gold={"prompt": ex["prompt"], "test": ex["test"], "entry_point": ex["entry_point"]},
                          messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Complete the following Python function. Return the full function (including the signature) "
            "in a single ```python code block.\n\n```python\n" + ex["prompt"] + "```"}]))

    # (5) Instruction following: IFEval (verifiable constraints), random 300 of 541.
    ife = load_dataset("google/IFEval", split="train")
    for ex in sample(ife, N["instr"]):
        items.append(dict(task="instr", id=f"ifeval{ex['key']}", max_tokens=768,
                          gold={"key": ex["key"], "instruction_id_list": ex["instruction_id_list"],
                                "kwargs": ex["kwargs"], "prompt": ex["prompt"]},
                          messages=[{"role": "user", "content": ex["prompt"]}]))

    # (6) Creative writing: Reddit WritingPrompts (test split), short stories judged by an LLM.
    wp = load_dataset("euclaise/writingprompts", split="test")
    wp = wp.filter(lambda e: e["prompt"].startswith("[ WP ]") and 40 < len(e["prompt"]) < 300)
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(wp, N["creative"])):
        p = ex["prompt"].replace("[ WP ]", "").strip()
        items.append(dict(task="creative", id=f"wp{i}", max_tokens=400, gold=None, messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Write a short story (about 200 words) based on this prompt:\n\n" + p}]))

    with open(OUT / "suite.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for it in items:
            f.write(json.dumps(it) + "\n")
    from collections import Counter
    print(Counter(it["task"] for it in items))
    for t in N:
        ex = next(it for it in items if it["task"] == t)
        print("----", t, "\n", ex["messages"][0]["content"][:300], "\nGOLD:", str(ex["gold"])[:150])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from datasets import load_dataset

SEED = 42
N = {"arith": 250, "factqa": 400, "reading": 400, "code": 164, "instr": 300, "creative": 100}
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "datasets"


def sample(ds, n, seed=SEED):
    idx = list(range(len(ds)))
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(idx)
    return [ds[i] for i in idx[:n]]


def main():
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    items = []

    # (1) Arithmetic reasoning: GSM8K test, zero-shot chain of thought.
    gsm = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="test")
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(gsm, N["arith"])):
        gold = ex["answer"].split("####")[-1].strip().replace(",", "")
        items.append(dict(task="arith", id=f"gsm{i}", max_tokens=512, gold=gold, messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            ex["question"] + "\n\nSolve the problem step by step. End your response with the line "
            "'The answer is N' where N is the final number."}]))

    # (2) Factual QA: TriviaQA (closed book), short answer, alias match.
    tqa = load_dataset("mandarjoshi/trivia_qa", "rc.nocontext", split="validation")
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(tqa, N["factqa"])):
        aliases = sorted(set(ex["answer"]["normalized_aliases"] + [ex["answer"]["normalized_value"]]))
        items.append(dict(task="factqa", id=f"tqa{i}", max_tokens=32, gold=aliases, messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Answer the trivia question with only the answer (a few words), no explanation.\n\nQuestion: "
            + ex["question"] + "\nAnswer:"}]))

    # (3) Reading comprehension: SQuAD v1.1 validation, extractive span.
    sq = load_dataset("rajpurkar/squad", split="validation")
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(sq, N["reading"])):
        items.append(dict(task="reading", id=f"squad{i}", max_tokens=32, gold=ex["answers"]["text"], messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Read the passage and answer the question with a short span copied from the passage. "
            "Reply with only the answer.\n\nPassage: " + ex["context"] + "\n\nQuestion: " + ex["question"] + "\nAnswer:"}]))

    # (4) Code generation: HumanEval (all 164), executed with unit tests.
    he = load_dataset("openai/openai_humaneval", split="test")
    for ex in he:
        items.append(dict(task="code", id=ex["task_id"], max_tokens=512,
                          gold={"prompt": ex["prompt"], "test": ex["test"], "entry_point": ex["entry_point"]},
                          messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Complete the following Python function. Return the full function (including the signature) "
            "in a single ```python code block.\n\n```python\n" + ex["prompt"] + "```"}]))

    # (5) Instruction following: IFEval (verifiable constraints), random 300 of 541.
    ife = load_dataset("google/IFEval", split="train")
    for ex in sample(ife, N["instr"]):
        items.append(dict(task="instr", id=f"ifeval{ex['key']}", max_tokens=768,
                          gold={"key": ex["key"], "instruction_id_list": ex["instruction_id_list"],
                                "kwargs": ex["kwargs"], "prompt": ex["prompt"]},
                          messages=[{"role": "user", "content": ex["prompt"]}]))

    # (6) Creative writing: Reddit WritingPrompts (test split), short stories judged by an LLM.
    wp = load_dataset("euclaise/writingprompts", split="test")
    wp = wp.filter(lambda e: e["prompt"].startswith("[ WP ]") and 40 < len(e["prompt"]) < 300)
    for i, ex in enumerate(sample(wp, N["creative"])):
        p = ex["prompt"].replace("[ WP ]", "").strip()
        items.append(dict(task="creative", id=f"wp{i}", max_tokens=400, gold=None, messages=[{"role": "user", "content":
            "Write a short story (about 200 words) based on this prompt:\n\n" + p}]))

    with open(OUT / "suite.jsonl", "w") as f:
        for it in items:
            f.write(json.dumps(it) + "\n")
    from collections import Counter
    print(Counter(it["task"] for it in items))
    for t in N:
        ex = next(it for it in items if it["task"] == t)
        print("----", t, "\n", ex["messages"][0]["content"][:300], "\nGOLD:", str(ex["gold"])[:150])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Weight-only round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization shared by the vLLM generation and HF KL scripts.

We simulate b-bit integer weight storage ("fake quantization"): each row of a linear
weight [out, in] is split into groups of `group` input channels; every group gets its own
asymmetric min-max scale/zero-point, the weights are rounded to the 2^b integer grid and
de-quantized back to bf16. Numerically this is exactly what an INT-b g128 kernel computes
(up to accumulation order), and it lets us sweep arbitrary bit widths with one code path.
Embeddings and the LM head stay in bf16 (standard practice in GPTQ/AWQ evaluations).
"""
import re

import torch

# Transformer-block linear layers in HF (q_proj, ..., down_proj) and vLLM (qkv_proj, gate_up_proj, ...)
LINEAR_RE = re.compile(r"layers\.\d+\..*(proj|fc\d?|dense|qkv|query_key_value)\.weight$")


@torch.no_grad()
def rtn_dequant(w: torch.Tensor, bits: int, group: int = 128) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return the RTN-quantized-then-dequantized copy of a 2-D weight (same dtype/device)."""
    if bits >= 16:
        return w
    out, inp = w.shape
    g = group if (group > 0 and inp % group == 0) else inp  # group<=0 -> per-output-channel
    qmax = 2 ** bits - 1
    res = torch.empty_like(w)
    rows = max(1, (1 << 26) // inp)  # chunk rows to bound fp32 temp memory (~256 MB)
    for s in range(0, out, rows):
        x = w[s:s + rows].float().reshape(-1, g)
        mn, mx = x.amin(1, keepdim=True), x.amax(1, keepdim=True)
        scale = (mx - mn).clamp(min=1e-8) / qmax
        zero = torch.round(-mn / scale)
        q = torch.clamp(torch.round(x / scale) + zero, 0, qmax)
        res[s:s + rows] = ((q - zero) * scale).reshape(-1, inp).to(w.dtype)
    return res


def quantizable(name: str, p: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
    return p.dim() == 2 and LINEAR_RE.search(name) is not None

"""Generate greedy outputs for the whole task suite at several RTN weight precisions.

One vLLM engine is created per model; between precision levels the transformer linear
weights are restored from a CPU backup and re-quantized in place inside the worker
(prefix caching disabled so no KV computed under other weights is reused).

Usage: python src/generate.py --model qwen1.5b --levels 16,8,6,5,4,3,2 --gpu_gb 5
Outputs: results/gens/{model}_b{bits}_g{group}.jsonl  (one line per suite item)
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = str(ROOT / "src")
sys.path.insert(0, SRC)
from models import MODELS  # noqa: E402


def _quantize_worker(self, bits, group, src):
    """Runs inside the vLLM worker: restore bf16 weights, then RTN-quantize to `bits`."""
    import sys
    import torch
    sys.path.insert(0, src)
    from quant import quantizable, rtn_dequant
    model = self.model_runner.model
    if not hasattr(self, "_qorig"):
        self._qorig = {n: p.detach().to("cpu", copy=True) for n, p in model.named_parameters() if quantizable(n, p)}
    n_q = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for n, p in model.named_parameters():
            if n in self._qorig:
                p.data.copy_(rtn_dequant(self._qorig[n].to(p.device), bits, group))
                n_q += 1
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return n_q, sorted(self._qorig)[:3]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--levels", default="16,8,6,5,4,3,2")
    ap.add_argument("--group", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--gpu_gb", type=float, default=12.0)
    ap.add_argument("--max_num_seqs", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--batched_tokens", type=int, default=4096)
    ap.add_argument("--eager", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="debug: items per task")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    import torch
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    repo, _, _ = MODELS[args.model]
    is_awq = args.model.endswith("-awq")
    levels = [4] if is_awq else [int(x) for x in args.levels.split(",")]
    outdir = ROOT / "results" / "gens"
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def outpath(b):
        tag = "awq" if is_awq else f"b{b}_g{args.group}"
        return outdir / f"{args.model}_{tag}.jsonl"

    todo = [b for b in levels if not outpath(b).exists()]
    if not todo:
        print("nothing to do"); return

    suite = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets" / "suite.jsonl")]
    if args.limit:
        from collections import defaultdict
        cnt = defaultdict(int); keep = []
        for it in suite:
            if cnt[it["task"]] < args.limit:
                keep.append(it); cnt[it["task"]] += 1
        suite = keep

    total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[1]
    llm = LLM(model=repo, dtype="bfloat16" if not is_awq else "auto", seed=0,
              gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_gb * 2**30 / total, max_model_len=2560,
              max_num_seqs=args.max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens=args.batched_tokens,
              enforce_eager=args.eager, enable_prefix_caching=False, trust_remote_code=False)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
    prompts = [tok.apply_chat_template(it["messages"], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) for it in suite]
    sps = [SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=it["max_tokens"], seed=0) for it in suite]

    for b in todo:
        t0 = time.time()
        if not is_awq:
            info = llm.collective_rpc(_quantize_worker, args=(b, args.group, SRC))
            print(f"[{args.model}] bits={b}: quantized {info[0][0]} matrices e.g. {info[0][1]}", flush=True)
            assert info[0][0] > 0
        outs = llm.generate(prompts, sps, use_tqdm=False)
        tmp = outpath(b).with_suffix(".partial")
        with open(tmp, "w") as f:
            for it, o in zip(suite, outs):
                c = o.outputs[0]
                f.write(json.dumps({"task": it["task"], "id": it["id"], "model": args.model,
                                    "bits": 4 if is_awq else b, "method": "awq" if is_awq else "rtn",
                                    "group": args.group, "response": c.text, "n_tokens": len(c.token_ids),
                                    "finish": c.finish_reason}) + "\n")
        if args.limit:
            print(outs[0].outputs[0].text[:500]); tmp.unlink(); continue
        tmp.rename(outpath(b))
        print(f"[{args.model}] bits={b} done in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Outputs: results/gens/{model}_b{bits}_g{group}.jsonl  (one line per suite item)
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = str(ROOT / "src")
sys.path.insert(0, SRC)
from models import MODELS  # noqa: E402


def _quantize_worker(self, bits, group, src):
    """Runs inside the vLLM worker: restore bf16 weights, then RTN-quantize to `bits`."""
    import sys
    import torch
    sys.path.insert(0, src)
    from quant import quantizable, rtn_dequant
    model = self.model_runner.model
    if not hasattr(self, "_qorig"):
        self._qorig = {n: p.detach().to("cpu", copy=True) for n, p in model.named_parameters() if quantizable(n, p)}
    n_q = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for n, p in model.named_parameters():
            if n in self._qorig:
                p.data.copy_(rtn_dequant(self._qorig[n].to(p.device), bits, group))
                n_q += 1
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return n_q, sorted(self._qorig)[:3]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--levels", default="16,8,6,5,4,3,2")
    ap.add_argument("--group", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--gpu_gb", type=float, default=12.0)
    ap.add_argument("--max_num_seqs", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--batched_tokens", type=int, default=4096)
    ap.add_argument("--eager", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="debug: items per task")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    import torch
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    repo, _, _ = MODELS[args.model]
    is_awq = args.model.endswith("-awq")
    levels = [4] if is_awq else [int(x) for x in args.levels.split(",")]
    outdir = ROOT / "results" / "gens"
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def outpath(b):
        tag = "awq" if is_awq else f"b{b}_g{args.group}"
        return outdir / f"{args.model}_{tag}.jsonl"

    todo = [b for b in levels if not outpath(b).exists()]
    if not todo:
        print("nothing to do"); return

    suite = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets" / "suite.jsonl")]
    if args.limit:
        from collections import defaultdict
        cnt = defaultdict(int); keep = []
        for it in suite:
            if cnt[it["task"]] < args.limit:
                keep.append(it); cnt[it["task"]] += 1
        suite = keep

    total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[1]
    llm = LLM(model=repo, dtype="bfloat16" if not is_awq else "auto", seed=0,
              gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_gb * 2**30 / total, max_model_len=2560,
              max_num_seqs=args.max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens=args.batched_tokens,
              enforce_eager=args.eager, enable_prefix_caching=False, trust_remote_code=False)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
    prompts = [tok.apply_chat_template(it["messages"], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) for it in suite]
    sps = [SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=it["max_tokens"], seed=0) for it in suite]

    for b in todo:
        t0 = time.time()
        if not is_awq:
            info = llm.collective_rpc(_quantize_worker, args=(b, args.group, SRC))
            print(f"[{args.model}] bits={b}: quantized {info[0][0]} matrices e.g. {info[0][1]}", flush=True)
            assert info[0][0] > 0
        outs = llm.generate(prompts, sps, use_tqdm=False)
        tmp = outpath(b).with_suffix(".partial")
        with open(tmp, "w") as f:
            for it, o in zip(suite, outs):
                c = o.outputs[0]
                f.write(json.dumps({"task": it["task"], "id": it["id"], "model": args.model,
                                    "bits": 4 if is_awq else b, "method": "awq" if is_awq else "rtn",
                                    "group": args.group, "response": c.text, "n_tokens": len(c.token_ids),
                                    "finish": c.finish_reason}) + "\n")
        if args.limit:
            print(outs[0].outputs[0].text[:500]); tmp.unlink(); continue
        tmp.rename(outpath(b))
        print(f"[{args.model}] bits={b} done in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Planning: Quantization Failure Modes — Task-Specific Accuracy Cliffs

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Weight-only post-training quantization (INT8/INT4, GPTQ, AWQ) is the default way to deploy LLMs
on commodity hardware. Practitioners usually pick a bit width from aggregate metrics (WikiText
perplexity, MMLU), but the damage may be very uneven across tasks: a model can look fine on
perplexity and still fail on multi-step arithmetic. A task-resolved map of *where* accuracy
collapses, and a cheap label-free signal that warns *before* it collapses, would let deployers
choose precision per use case.

### Gap in Existing Work
(No literature review was pre-gathered for this run; this is based on prior knowledge.)
GPTQ (Frantar et al., 2022) and AWQ (Lin et al., 2024) report perplexity plus a few zero-shot
multiple-choice tasks, mostly at 3–4 bits. Follow-up evaluations (e.g. "Evaluating Quantized
LLMs", Li et al. 2024; Jin et al. 2024; Marchisio et al. 2024 on multilingual quantization) show
uneven degradation, but (a) rarely sweep bit width finely enough to locate a cliff, (b) rarely
mix generative tasks (code, instruction following, creative writing) with QA under one protocol,
and (c) do not test whether distribution-level divergence (KL from the full-precision model)
anticipates the accuracy cliff. Dutta et al. (2024, "Accuracy is not all you need") argue for
KL/"flips" as complementary metrics, but do not test KL as a leading indicator of task cliffs.

### Our Novel Contribution
A controlled sweep: 8 instruction-tuned models from 3 families (Qwen2.5 0.5B–14B, Llama-3.2-1B /
Llama-3.1-8B, Phi-3-mini) × 7 weight precisions (bf16, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 bits; RTN, group 128) ×
6 task types, with task-specific token-level KL from the bf16 model measured on the
same task distributions. We explicitly test cliff location, task ordering, size dependence and
the "KL ≈ 0.3 nats" early-warning claim.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (accuracy sweep): needed to locate cliffs per task/model; directly tests H1, H2, H3.
- Exp 2 (task-specific KL + WikiText perplexity): tests H4 (KL as a leading indicator) and
  compares KL to the standard perplexity proxy.
- Exp 3 (real AWQ INT4 checkpoints for Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B): checks that RTN-INT4 conclusions
  transfer to a production quantizer (RTN is a pessimistic lower bound).
- Exp 4 (robustness: per-channel vs group-128 at 4/3 bits on a subset): tests whether cliff
  location depends on quantization granularity rather than on "bits" per se.

## Research Question
Which task types lose accuracy first as weight precision is lowered, is the loss gradual or a
cliff, does the cliff move to higher precision for smaller models, and does KL divergence from the
full-precision model predict the cliff before accuracy degrades?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: Arithmetic (GSM8K) and factual QA (TriviaQA) show a >15% (relative) accuracy drop between
  INT8 and INT4.
- H2: Creative writing (judge score) and reading comprehension (SQuAD F1) retain ≥85% of bf16
  performance at INT4.
- H3: Within a family, the smaller the model, the higher the bit width at which the cliff occurs
  (critical bits negatively correlated with log parameter count).
- H4: Mean token-level KL(bf16 || quantized) crosses ≈0.3 nats at or before the precision at which
  the accuracy cliff appears; KL at level b predicts a cliff at level b or b−1.

Independent variables: bit width, task, model (size, family). Dependent: task score, retained
fraction (score_b / score_bf16), KL, top-1 agreement, perplexity.

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
Local models only (no API keys on this host; Ollama not available — vLLM + HF transformers
instead). Weight-only RTN asymmetric min-max quantization with group size 128 applied in place to
all transformer linear layers (embeddings / LM head kept bf16), implemented once (`src/quant.py`)
and used by both the vLLM generation and the HF KL code. RTN is chosen because it allows any bit
width with one code path and no calibration data (no confound from calibration-set choice); real
AWQ-INT4 is added as a reference.

### Experimental Steps
1. Build fixed suite (seed 42): GSM8K 250, TriviaQA 400, SQuAD 400, HumanEval 164, IFEval 300,
   WritingPrompts 100.
2. Greedy generation for every model × level (vLLM, temperature 0).
3. Score: GSM8K exact numeric match; TriviaQA alias match (normalized containment); SQuAD token F1
   (and EM); HumanEval pass@1 via sandboxed execution; IFEval prompt-level strict accuracy;
   creative: LLM judge (Qwen local model, 1–10 rubric) + repetition statistics.
4. KL: teacher-force the bf16 model's own responses (first 60 items per task) through each
   quantized model; KL over response tokens using bf16 top-128 + lumped tail bucket (a lower bound
   on true KL); also WikiText-2 perplexity.
5. Analysis: cliffs, critical bits, correlations, logistic / threshold analysis for KL.

### Baselines
bf16 model (reference for every metric); AWQ-INT4 (production quantizer); 8-bit as the "safe"
reference level for cliff definitions.

### Evaluation Metrics
Task scores above; retained fraction; relative drop between adjacent levels; cliff = relative drop
>15% between adjacent tested precisions (with absolute drop also reported); critical bits = highest
precision with retained fraction < 0.85.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
Bootstrap 95% CIs (1000 resamples over items) for scores; paired McNemar (binary tasks) / paired
Wilcoxon (F1, judge scores) between bf16 and each level, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR at 0.05; Spearman
correlation of critical bits with log size; for H4, ROC-AUC of KL for predicting "retained < 0.85",
best threshold by Youden's J with bootstrap CI, and lead-time analysis (KL at the last "healthy"
level vs at the cliff level).

## Expected Outcomes
Supporting H1: GSM8K/TriviaQA retained < 0.85 at 4 bits. Refuting: retained ≥ 0.85 at 4 bits
(cliff at 3 bits or lower). H4 supported if KL threshold ≈0.3 with high AUC and KL elevated at the
level preceding the cliff.

## Timeline and Milestones
Setup+data 30 min; generation ~2–3 h (shared GPUs); KL ~1 h; scoring+judge ~1 h; analysis+report 1 h.

## Potential Challenges
Shared GPUs (memory fluctuates) → retry queues, small slices for small models. 2-bit outputs are
garbage and slow (max tokens) → accepted cost. Judge bias toward fluent text → also report
repetition/degeneration statistics. Note: "INT8 vs INT4" in the hypothesis is interpreted for
RTN-g128; we add 6/5/3/2 bits to localize cliffs.

## Success Criteria
All model × level × task cells scored, KL computed for each, every hypothesis given a clear
supported / partially supported / refuted verdict with CIs.

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Weight-only post-training quantization (INT8/INT4, GPTQ, AWQ) is the default way to deploy LLMs

collapses, and a cheap label-free signal that warns *before* it collapses, would let deployers
choose precision per use case.

multiple-choice tasks, mostly at 3–4 bits. Follow-up evaluations (e.g. "Evaluating Quantized
LLMs", Li et al. 2024; Jin et al. 2024; Marchisio et al. 2024 on multilingual quantization) show

anticipates the accuracy cliff. Dutta et al. (2024, "Accuracy is not all you need") argue for

#!/bin/bash
# Usage: gpu_queue.sh "GPU_LIST" GPU_GB "EXTRA_ARGS" -- model1 model2 ...
# For each model: wait until one of the GPUs in GPU_LIST has > GPU_GB+0.7 GB free, then run
# generate.py there. Waiting does not consume retries; only real failures do (max 8).
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."; source .venv/bin/activate
GPUS=$1; GB=$2; EXTRA=$3; shift 4
need=$(python -c "print(int(($GB+0.7)*1024))")
for m in "$@"; do
  fails=0
  while [ $fails -lt 8 ]; do
    gpu=""
    while [ -z "$gpu" ]; do
      for g in $GPUS; do
        f=$(nvidia-smi -i $g --query-gpu=memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits)
        if [ "$f" -gt "$need" ]; then gpu=$g; break; fi
      done
      [ -z "$gpu" ] && sleep 30
    done
    echo "$(date) $m start on GPU $gpu" >> logs/gen_$m.log
    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$gpu python src/generate.py --model $m --gpu_gb $GB $EXTRA >> logs/gen_$m.log 2>&1 && break
    fails=$((fails+1)); echo "$(date) $m fail $fails" >> logs/gen_$m.log; sleep 20
  done
  echo "$(date) $m finished (fails=$fails)" >> logs/queue_status.txt
done
EOF
chmod +x src/gpu_queue.sh

"""Task-specific token-level KL(bf16 || quantized), top-1 agreement, output NLL and WikiText-2 PPL.

For each task we teacher-force the bf16 model's own greedy responses (first N items per task,
response truncated to 256 tokens) and compare next-token distributions on response tokens.
The bf16 distribution is stored as top-K (K=128) log-probs; KL is computed over those K tokens
plus one lumped "tail" bucket. By the data-processing inequality this is a lower bound on the
exact KL; `--validate` measures the gap against exact KL on a few sequences.

Usage: python src/kl.py --model qwen1.5b [--levels 16,8,6,5,4,3,2] [--group 128]
Output: results/kl/{model}_g{group}.csv  (rows: level x task, incl. task="wikitext")
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")
import pandas as pd
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from models import MODELS  # noqa: E402
from quant import quantizable, rtn_dequant  # noqa: E402

K = 128
TASKS = ["arith", "factqa", "reading", "code", "instr", "creative"]


def build_sequences(tok, model_key, n_per_task, max_resp=256):
    suite = {json.loads(l)["id"]: json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "datasets" / "suite.jsonl")}
    gens = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "results" / "gens" / f"{model_key}_b16_g128.jsonl")]
    seqs, cnt = [], {t: 0 for t in TASKS}
    for g in gens:
        if cnt[g["task"]] >= n_per_task:
            continue
        p_ids = tok.apply_chat_template(suite[g["id"]]["messages"], add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True)
        if isinstance(p_ids, dict) or hasattr(p_ids, "input_ids"):
            p_ids = p_ids["input_ids"]
        r_ids = tok(g["response"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"][:max_resp]
        if len(r_ids) < 1:
            continue
        cnt[g["task"]] += 1
        seqs.append(dict(task=g["task"], ids=torch.tensor(p_ids + r_ids), n_resp=len(r_ids)))
    return seqs


def wikitext_windows(tok, n_windows, win=1024):
    from datasets import load_dataset
    ds = load_dataset("Salesforce/wikitext", "wikitext-2-raw-v1", split="test")
    ids = tok("\n\n".join(ds["text"]), add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    return [dict(task="wikitext", ids=torch.tensor(ids[i * win:(i + 1) * win]), n_resp=win - 1) for i in range(n_windows)]


@torch.no_grad()
def resp_logprobs(model, s, dev):
    """Log-probs (fp32) predicting each of the last n_resp tokens: shape [n_resp, V]."""
    ids = s["ids"].to(dev)[None]
    out = model(ids, logits_to_keep=s["n_resp"] + 1)
    logits = out.logits[0, :-1].float()  # positions predicting the last n_resp tokens
    return F.log_softmax(logits, -1), ids[0, -s["n_resp"]:]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--levels", default="16,8,6,5,4,3,2")
    ap.add_argument("--group", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--n_per_task", type=int, default=60)
    ap.add_argument("--wiki_windows", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--validate", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    dev = "cuda"
    out_path = ROOT / "results" / "kl" / f"{args.model}_g{args.group}.csv"
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    repo = MODELS[args.model][0]
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(dev).eval()
    seqs = build_sequences(tok, args.model, args.n_per_task) + wikitext_windows(tok, args.wiki_windows)
    print(f"{len(seqs)} sequences, {sum(s['n_resp'] for s in seqs)} scored tokens", flush=True)
    orig = {n: p.detach().to("cpu", copy=True) for n, p in model.named_parameters() if quantizable(n, p)}
    print(f"{len(orig)} quantizable matrices", flush=True)

    # Reference pass (bf16): store top-K log-probs and argmax per position.
    ref = []
    exact_ref = []
    for i, s in enumerate(seqs):
        lp, tgt = resp_logprobs(model, s, dev)
        v, ix = lp.topk(K, -1)
        ref.append((v.cpu(), ix.cpu()))
        if args.validate and i % 50 == 0 and len(exact_ref) < 6:
            exact_ref.append((i, lp.cpu()))

    rows = []
    for b in [int(x) for x in args.levels.split(",")]:
        t0 = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for n, p in model.named_parameters():
                if n in orig:
                    p.data.copy_(rtn_dequant(orig[n].to(dev), b, args.group))
        acc = {}
        for i, s in enumerate(seqs):
            lq, tgt = resp_logprobs(model, s, dev)
            pv, pix = ref[i][0].to(dev), ref[i][1].to(dev)
            p = pv.exp()
            qv = lq.gather(1, pix)
            r_p = (1 - p.sum(1)).clamp(min=1e-12)
            r_q = (1 - qv.exp().sum(1)).clamp(min=1e-12)
            kl_tok = (p * (pv - qv)).sum(1) + r_p * (r_p.log() - r_q.log())
            kl_tok = kl_tok.clamp(min=0)
            nll = -lq.gather(1, tgt[:, None])[:, 0]
            agree = (lq.argmax(1) == pix[:, 0]).float()
            a = acc.setdefault(s["task"], dict(kl=0.0, nll=0.0, agree=0.0, n=0, seq_kl=[], kl_max=[]))
            a["kl"] += kl_tok.sum().item(); a["nll"] += nll.sum().item(); a["agree"] += agree.sum().item()
            a["n"] += len(kl_tok); a["seq_kl"].append(kl_tok.mean().item())
            if args.validate:
                for j, lp_exact in exact_ref:
                    if j == i:
                        ex = (lp_exact.exp() * (lp_exact - lq.cpu())).sum(1).mean().item()
                        print(f"  validate bits={b} seq{i}: exact KL={ex:.4f} topK-bound={kl_tok.mean().item():.4f}")
        for t, a in acc.items():
            rows.append(dict(model=args.model, bits=b, group=args.group, task=t, kl=a["kl"] / a["n"],
                             kl_seqmean=sum(a["seq_kl"]) / len(a["seq_kl"]), top1_agree=a["agree"] / a["n"],
                             nll=a["nll"] / a["n"], ppl=math.exp(min(50, a["nll"] / a["n"])), n_tokens=a["n"],
                             n_seqs=len(a["seq_kl"])))
        print(f"[{args.model}] bits={b} ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s): " +
              " ".join(f"{r['task']}:{r['kl']:.3f}" for r in rows if r["bits"] == b), flush=True)
        pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(out_path.with_suffix(".partial"), index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(out_path, index=False)
    out_path.with_suffix(".partial").unlink()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The bf16 distribution is stored as top-K (K=128) log-probs; KL is computed over those K tokens
plus one lumped "tail" bucket. By the data-processing inequality this is a lower bound on the
exact KL; `--validate` measures the gap against exact KL on a few sequences.

    gens = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ROOT / "results" / "gens" / f"{model_key}_b16_g128.jsonl")]
    seqs, cnt = [], {t: 0 for t in TASKS}
    for g in gens:
        if cnt[g["task"]] >= n_per_task:
            continue
        p_ids = tok.apply_chat_template(suite[g["id"]]["messages"], add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True)
        if isinstance(p_ids, dict) or hasattr(p_ids, "input_ids"):
            p_ids = p_ids["input_ids"]
        r_ids = tok(g["response"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"][:max_resp]
        if len(r_ids) < 1:
            continue
        cnt[g["task"]] += 1
        seqs.append(dict(task=g["task"], ids=torch.tensor(p_ids + r_ids), n_resp=len(r_ids)))

"""Aggregate scores + KL and test hypotheses H1-H4. Writes tables to results/ and figures to figures/.

Definitions (pre-registered in planning.md)
- retained(b) = score(b) / score(bf16) for a (model, task).
- cliff between adjacent tested precisions b_hi > b_lo: retained(b_hi) - retained(b_lo) > 0.15.
- critical bits = highest precision whose retained fraction < 0.85 (bits "1" = never failed).
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from statsmodels.stats.contingency_tables import mcnemar
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from models import MODELS, LEVELS  # noqa: E402

RES, FIG = ROOT / "results", ROOT / "figures"
FIG.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
TASKS = ["arith", "factqa", "code", "instr", "reading", "creative"]
TNAME = {"arith": "Arithmetic (GSM8K)", "factqa": "Factual QA (TriviaQA)", "code": "Code (HumanEval)",
         "instr": "Instruction following (IFEval)", "reading": "Reading comp. (SQuAD F1)",
         "creative": "Creative writing (judge)"}
SWEEP = [m for m in MODELS if not m.endswith("-awq")]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)


def load_items():
    df = pd.read_csv(RES / "item_scores.csv")
    jc = {}
    if (RES / "judge_cache.jsonl").exists():
        for l in open(RES / "judge_cache.jsonl"):
            r = json.loads(l)
            jc[r["key"]] = np.mean(list(r["scores"].values())) / 10 if r["scores"] else np.nan
    m = df.task == "creative"
    keys = df[m].model + "|" + df[m].method + "|" + df[m].bits.astype(str) + "|" + df[m].group.astype(str) + "|" + df[m].id
    df.loc[m, "score"] = keys.map(jc).values
    return df


def boot_ci(x, n=1000):
    x = np.asarray(x, float); x = x[~np.isnan(x)]
    if len(x) == 0:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    bs = rng.choice(x, (n, len(x))).mean(1)
    return np.percentile(bs, 2.5), np.percentile(bs, 97.5)


def summarize(df):
    rows = []
    for (mo, me, b, g, t), d in df.groupby(["model", "method", "bits", "group", "task"]):
        lo, hi = boot_ci(d.score)
        rows.append(dict(model=mo, method=me, bits=b, group=g, task=t, score=d.score.mean(), ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi,
                         n=d.score.notna().sum(), trunc_rate=d.truncated.mean(), distinct2=d.distinct2.mean()))
    s = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    base = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.bits == 16) & (s.group == 128)].set_index(["model", "task"]).score
    s["base_model"] = s.model.str.replace("-awq", "")
    s["retained"] = [r.score / base.get((r.base_model, r.task), np.nan) for r in s.itertuples()]
    s["family"] = s.base_model.map(lambda m: MODELS[m][1])
    s["params_b"] = s.base_model.map(lambda m: MODELS[m][2])
    return s


def paired_tests(df):
    """bf16 vs each level: McNemar (binary tasks) or Wilcoxon (continuous), BH-FDR across all tests."""
    rows = []
    d0 = df[(df.method == "rtn") & (df.group == 128)]
    for (mo, t), d in d0.groupby(["model", "task"]):
        piv = d.pivot_table(index="id", columns="bits", values="score")
        if 16 not in piv:
            continue
        for b in [x for x in LEVELS if x != 16 and x in piv]:
            pr = piv[[16, b]].dropna()
            if t in ("arith", "factqa", "code", "instr"):
                tab = pd.crosstab(pr[16] > 0.5, pr[b] > 0.5).reindex(index=[False, True], columns=[False, True], fill_value=0)
                p = mcnemar(tab.values, exact=True).pvalue
            else:
                diff = pr[16] - pr[b]
                p = 1.0 if (diff == 0).all() else stats.wilcoxon(pr[16], pr[b]).pvalue
            rows.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, bits=b, delta=pr[b].mean() - pr[16].mean(), p=p, n=len(pr)))
    r = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    r["p_bh"] = multipletests(r.p, method="fdr_bh")[1]
    r["sig"] = r.p_bh < 0.05
    return r


def cliffs(s):
    rows = []
    sw = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)]
    for (mo, t), d in sw.groupby(["model", "task"]):
        d = d.set_index("bits").retained.reindex(LEVELS)
        drops = {f"{hi}->{lo}": d[hi] - d[lo] for hi, lo in zip(LEVELS[:-1], LEVELS[1:])}
        crit = next((b for b in LEVELS if d[b] < 0.85), 1)
        big = max(drops, key=drops.get)
        rows.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, family=MODELS[mo][1], params_b=MODELS[mo][2], critical_bits=crit,
                         largest_drop_step=big, largest_drop=drops[big], drop_8_to_4=d[8] - d[4],
                         cliff_8_to_4=(d[8] - d[4]) > 0.15, ret8=d[8], ret6=d[6], ret5=d[5], ret4=d[4], ret3=d[3], ret2=d[2],
                         any_cliff_steps=",".join(k for k, v in drops.items() if v > 0.15)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def kl_analysis(s, cl):
    kls = [pd.read_csv(p) for p in sorted((RES / "kl").glob("*_g128.csv"))]
    if not kls:
        return None, {}
    kl = pd.concat(kls)
    wiki = kl[kl.task == "wikitext"][["model", "bits", "ppl"]].rename(columns={"ppl": "wiki_ppl"})
    w16 = wiki[wiki.bits == 16].set_index("model").wiki_ppl
    wiki["wiki_ppl_ratio"] = wiki.wiki_ppl / wiki.model.map(w16)
    m = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)].merge(kl[kl.task != "wikitext"], on=["model", "bits", "task"]) \
        .merge(wiki, on=["model", "bits"])
    m = m[m.bits != 16].copy()
    m["failed"] = m.retained < 0.85
    out = {"n_cells": len(m), "n_failed": int(m.failed.sum())}
    out["spearman_kl_retained"] = stats.spearmanr(m.kl, m.retained)._asdict()
    for col, sign in [("kl", 1), ("wiki_ppl_ratio", 1), ("top1_agree", -1)]:
        out[f"auc_{col}"] = roc_auc_score(m.failed, sign * m[col])
    # Optimal KL threshold (Youden J) with bootstrap CI.
    def youden(df):
        ths = np.unique(df.kl)
        best = max(ths, key=lambda th: ((df.kl >= th) & df.failed).sum() / max(1, df.failed.sum())
                   - ((df.kl >= th) & ~df.failed).sum() / max(1, (~df.failed).sum()))
        return best
    th = youden(m)
    bs = [youden(m.sample(len(m), replace=True, random_state=i)) for i in range(300)]
    out["youden_threshold"] = float(th); out["youden_ci"] = [float(np.percentile(bs, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(bs, 97.5))]
    for t0 in [0.3, th]:
        pred = m.kl >= t0
        out[f"at_{t0:.3f}"] = dict(sensitivity=float((pred & m.failed).sum() / max(1, m.failed.sum())),
                                   specificity=float((~pred & ~m.failed).sum() / max(1, (~m.failed).sum())))
    out["per_task_auc"] = {t: (roc_auc_score(d.failed, d.kl) if d.failed.nunique() == 2 else None)
                           for t, d in m.groupby("task")}
    out["kl_at_failure_by_task_median"] = m[m.failed].groupby("task").kl.median().to_dict()
    out["kl_at_healthy_by_task_median"] = m[~m.failed].groupby("task").kl.median().to_dict()
    # Lead-indicator test: for each (model, task) with a failure, KL at the last healthy level above it.
    lead = []
    for (mo, t), d in m.groupby(["model", "task"]):
        d = d.set_index("bits").reindex([b for b in LEVELS if b != 16])
        crit = next((b for b in d.index if d.loc[b, "failed"] is True or d.loc[b, "failed"] == 1), None)
        if crit is None:
            continue
        i = list(d.index).index(crit)
        prev = d.index[i - 1] if i > 0 else None
        lead.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, critical_bits=crit, kl_at_crit=d.loc[crit, "kl"],
                         prev_bits=prev, kl_prev=d.loc[prev, "kl"] if prev else np.nan,
                         ret_prev=d.loc[prev, "retained"] if prev else np.nan))
    lead = pd.DataFrame(lead)
    out["lead_n"] = len(lead)
    out["lead_frac_prev_kl_ge_0.3"] = float((lead.kl_prev >= 0.3).mean())
    out["lead_frac_crit_kl_ge_0.3"] = float((lead.kl_at_crit >= 0.3).mean())
    out["lead_median_kl_prev"] = float(lead.kl_prev.median()); out["lead_median_kl_crit"] = float(lead.kl_at_crit.median())
    lead.to_csv(RES / "kl_lead_analysis.csv", index=False)
    m.to_csv(RES / "kl_vs_accuracy.csv", index=False)
    return m, out


def plot_curves(s):
    sw = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 8.5), sharex=True, sharey=True)
    xs = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(LEVELS)}
    cmap = {"Qwen2.5": plt.cm.Blues, "Llama-3": plt.cm.Oranges, "Phi-3": plt.cm.Greens}
    for ax, t in zip(axes.flat, TASKS):
        for mo in SWEEP:
            d = sw[(sw.model == mo) & (sw.task == t)].set_index("bits").reindex(LEVELS)
            if d.retained.isna().all():
                continue
            fam = MODELS[mo][1]
            fam_models = [x for x in SWEEP if MODELS[x][1] == fam]
            shade = 0.45 + 0.5 * fam_models.index(mo) / max(1, len(fam_models) - 1)
            ax.plot([xs[b] for b in LEVELS], d.retained.values, "-o", ms=4, color=cmap[fam](shade),
                    label=f"{fam} {MODELS[mo][2]:.1f}B")
            awq = s[(s.model == mo + "-awq") & (s.task == t)]
            if len(awq):
                ax.plot(xs[4] + 0.12, awq.retained.iloc[0], "*", ms=11, color=cmap[fam](shade), mec="k", mew=0.5)
        ax.axhline(0.85, ls="--", c="gray", lw=1)
        ax.axvspan(xs[8], xs[4], color="gray", alpha=0.06)
        ax.set_title(TNAME[t]); ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.25); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(LEVELS))); ax.set_xticklabels(["bf16" if b == 16 else f"{b}b" for b in LEVELS])
    axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("score / bf16 score"); axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("score / bf16 score")
    for ax in axes[1]:
        ax.set_xlabel("weight precision (RTN, group 128)")
    h, l = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(h, l, loc="lower center", ncol=8, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))
    fig.suptitle("Retained task performance vs weight precision (dashed: 85% threshold; ★: real AWQ-INT4 checkpoint)")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.04, 1, 1))
    fig.savefig(FIG / "fig1_retained_vs_bits.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def plot_heatmap(cl):
    piv = cl.pivot(index="model", columns="task", values="critical_bits").reindex(index=SWEEP, columns=TASKS)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 4.8))
    im = ax.imshow(piv.values, cmap="Reds", vmin=1, vmax=8)
    for i in range(piv.shape[0]):
        for j in range(piv.shape[1]):
            v = piv.values[i, j]
            ax.text(j, i, "none" if v == 1 else f"{int(v)}b", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9,
                    color="white" if v >= 5 else "black")
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(TASKS))); ax.set_xticklabels([TNAME[t].split(" (")[0] for t in TASKS], rotation=25, ha="right")
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(SWEEP))); ax.set_yticklabels([f"{MODELS[m][1]} {MODELS[m][2]:.1f}B" for m in SWEEP])
    ax.set_title("Critical precision: highest bit width with <85% of bf16 score")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="bits"); fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIG / "fig2_critical_bits_heatmap.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def plot_kl(m, out):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.8))
    ax = axes[0]
    mk = dict(zip(TASKS, "osD^vP"))
    for t in TASKS:
        d = m[m.task == t]
        ax.scatter(d.kl.clip(lower=1e-4), d.retained, s=18, marker=mk[t], label=TNAME[t].split(" (")[0], alpha=0.75)
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.axhline(0.85, ls="--", c="gray"); ax.axvline(0.3, ls=":", c="r", label="KL = 0.3 nats")
    ax.axvline(out["youden_threshold"], ls="-.", c="k", lw=1, label=f"best threshold {out['youden_threshold']:.2f}")
    ax.set_xlabel("task-specific KL(bf16 || quantized), nats/token"); ax.set_ylabel("retained score")
    ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.3); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.set_title("KL vs retained accuracy (all model×task×level)")
    ax = axes[1]
    sw = m.groupby(["bits", "task"]).kl.median().unstack().reindex([b for b in LEVELS if b != 16])
    for t in TASKS:
        if t in sw:
            ax.plot(range(len(sw)), sw[t], "-o", label=TNAME[t].split(" (")[0])
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(sw))); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{b}b" for b in sw.index]); ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.axhline(0.3, ls=":", c="r"); ax.set_ylabel("median KL across models (nats/token)"); ax.set_xlabel("weight precision")
    ax.set_title("KL grows ~4x per removed bit"); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(FIG / "fig3_kl_vs_accuracy.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def main():
    df = load_items()
    s = summarize(df)
    s.to_csv(RES / "summary_scores.csv", index=False)
    tests = paired_tests(df); tests.to_csv(RES / "paired_tests.csv", index=False)
    cl = cliffs(s); cl.to_csv(RES / "cliffs.csv", index=False)

"""Aggregate scores + KL and test hypotheses H1-H4. Writes tables to results/ and figures to figures/.

- retained(b) = score(b) / score(bf16) for a (model, task).
- cliff between adjacent tested precisions b_hi > b_lo: retained(b_hi) - retained(b_lo) > 0.15.
- critical bits = highest precision whose retained fraction < 0.85 (bits "1" = never failed).

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
from statsmodels.stats.contingency_tables import mcnemar
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "src"))
from models import MODELS, LEVELS  # noqa: E402

RES, FIG = ROOT / "results", ROOT / "figures"
FIG.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
TASKS = ["arith", "factqa", "code", "instr", "reading", "creative"]
TNAME = {"arith": "Arithmetic (GSM8K)", "factqa": "Factual QA (TriviaQA)", "code": "Code (HumanEval)",
         "instr": "Instruction following (IFEval)", "reading": "Reading comp. (SQuAD F1)",
         "creative": "Creative writing (judge)"}
SWEEP = [m for m in MODELS if not m.endswith("-awq")]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)


def load_items():
    df = pd.read_csv(RES / "item_scores.csv")
    jc = {}
    if (RES / "judge_cache.jsonl").exists():
        for l in open(RES / "judge_cache.jsonl"):
            r = json.loads(l)
            jc[r["key"]] = np.mean(list(r["scores"].values())) / 10 if r["scores"] else np.nan
    m = df.task == "creative"
    keys = df[m].model + "|" + df[m].method + "|" + df[m].bits.astype(str) + "|" + df[m].group.astype(str) + "|" + df[m].id
    df.loc[m, "score"] = keys.map(jc).values
    return df


def boot_ci(x, n=1000):
    x = np.asarray(x, float); x = x[~np.isnan(x)]
    if len(x) == 0:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    bs = rng.choice(x, (n, len(x))).mean(1)
    return np.percentile(bs, 2.5), np.percentile(bs, 97.5)


def summarize(df):
    rows = []
    for (mo, me, b, g, t), d in df.groupby(["model", "method", "bits", "group", "task"]):
        lo, hi = boot_ci(d.score)
        rows.append(dict(model=mo, method=me, bits=b, group=g, task=t, score=d.score.mean(), ci_lo=lo, ci_hi=hi,
                         n=d.score.notna().sum(), trunc_rate=d.truncated.mean(), distinct2=d.distinct2.mean()))
    s = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    base = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.bits == 16) & (s.group == 128)].set_index(["model", "task"]).score
    s["base_model"] = s.model.str.replace("-awq", "")
    s["retained"] = [r.score / base.get((r.base_model, r.task), np.nan) for r in s.itertuples()]
    s["family"] = s.base_model.map(lambda m: MODELS[m][1])
    s["params_b"] = s.base_model.map(lambda m: MODELS[m][2])
    return s


def paired_tests(df):
    """bf16 vs each level: McNemar (binary tasks) or Wilcoxon (continuous), BH-FDR across all tests."""
    rows = []
    d0 = df[(df.method == "rtn") & (df.group == 128)]
    for (mo, t), d in d0.groupby(["model", "task"]):
        piv = d.pivot_table(index="id", columns="bits", values="score")
        if 16 not in piv:
            continue
        for b in [x for x in LEVELS if x != 16 and x in piv]:
            pr = piv[[16, b]].dropna()
            if t in ("arith", "factqa", "code", "instr"):
                tab = pd.crosstab(pr[16] > 0.5, pr[b] > 0.5).reindex(index=[False, True], columns=[False, True], fill_value=0)
                p = mcnemar(tab.values, exact=True).pvalue
            else:
                diff = pr[16] - pr[b]
                p = 1.0 if (diff == 0).all() else stats.wilcoxon(pr[16], pr[b]).pvalue
            rows.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, bits=b, delta=pr[b].mean() - pr[16].mean(), p=p, n=len(pr)))
    r = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    r["p_bh"] = multipletests(r.p, method="fdr_bh")[1]
    r["sig"] = r.p_bh < 0.05
    return r


def cliffs(s):
    rows = []
    sw = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)]
    for (mo, t), d in sw.groupby(["model", "task"]):
        d = d.set_index("bits").retained.reindex(LEVELS)
        drops = {f"{hi}->{lo}": d[hi] - d[lo] for hi, lo in zip(LEVELS[:-1], LEVELS[1:])}
        crit = next((b for b in LEVELS if d[b] < 0.85), 1)
        big = max(drops, key=drops.get)
        rows.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, family=MODELS[mo][1], params_b=MODELS[mo][2], critical_bits=crit,
                         largest_drop_step=big, largest_drop=drops[big], drop_8_to_4=d[8] - d[4],
                         cliff_8_to_4=(d[8] - d[4]) > 0.15, ret8=d[8], ret6=d[6], ret5=d[5], ret4=d[4], ret3=d[3], ret2=d[2],
                         any_cliff_steps=",".join(k for k, v in drops.items() if v > 0.15)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def kl_analysis(s, cl):
    kls = [pd.read_csv(p) for p in sorted((RES / "kl").glob("*_g128.csv"))]
    if not kls:
        return None, {}
    kl = pd.concat(kls)
    wiki = kl[kl.task == "wikitext"][["model", "bits", "ppl"]].rename(columns={"ppl": "wiki_ppl"})
    w16 = wiki[wiki.bits == 16].set_index("model").wiki_ppl
    wiki["wiki_ppl_ratio"] = wiki.wiki_ppl / wiki.model.map(w16)
    m = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)].merge(kl[kl.task != "wikitext"], on=["model", "bits", "task"]) \
        .merge(wiki, on=["model", "bits"])
    m = m[m.bits != 16].copy()
    m["failed"] = m.retained < 0.85
    out = {"n_cells": len(m), "n_failed": int(m.failed.sum())}
    out["spearman_kl_retained"] = stats.spearmanr(m.kl, m.retained)._asdict()
    for col, sign in [("kl", 1), ("wiki_ppl_ratio", 1), ("top1_agree", -1)]:
        out[f"auc_{col}"] = roc_auc_score(m.failed, sign * m[col])

    def youden(df):
        ths = np.unique(df.kl)
        best = max(ths, key=lambda th: ((df.kl >= th) & df.failed).sum() / max(1, df.failed.sum())
                   - ((df.kl >= th) & ~df.failed).sum() / max(1, (~df.failed).sum()))
        return best

        pred = m.kl >= t0

                                   specificity=float((~pred & ~m.failed).sum() / max(1, (~m.failed).sum())))
    out["per_task_auc"] = {t: (roc_auc_score(d.failed, d.kl) if d.failed.nunique() == 2 else None)
                           for t, d in m.groupby("task")}
    out["kl_at_failure_by_task_median"] = m[m.failed].groupby("task").kl.median().to_dict()
    out["kl_at_healthy_by_task_median"] = m[~m.failed].groupby("task").kl.median().to_dict()

    lead = []

        if crit is None:

        prev = d.index[i - 1] if i > 0 else None
        lead.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, critical_bits=crit, kl_at_crit=d.loc[crit, "kl"],
                         prev_bits=prev, kl_prev=d.loc[prev, "kl"] if prev else np.nan,
                         ret_prev=d.loc[prev, "retained"] if prev else np.nan))
    lead = pd.DataFrame(lead)
    out["lead_n"] = len(lead)
    out["lead_frac_prev_kl_ge_0.3"] = float((lead.kl_prev >= 0.3).mean())
    out["lead_frac_crit_kl_ge_0.3"] = float((lead.kl_at_crit >= 0.3).mean())
    out["lead_median_kl_prev"] = float(lead.kl_prev.median()); out["lead_median_kl_crit"] = float(lead.kl_at_crit.median())
    lead.to_csv(RES / "kl_lead_analysis.csv", index=False)
    m.to_csv(RES / "kl_vs_accuracy.csv", index=False)

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 8.5), sharex=True, sharey=True)
    xs = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(LEVELS)}
    cmap = {"Qwen2.5": plt.cm.Blues, "Llama-3": plt.cm.Oranges, "Phi-3": plt.cm.Greens}
    for ax, t in zip(axes.flat, TASKS):

            d = sw[(sw.model == mo) & (sw.task == t)].set_index("bits").reindex(LEVELS)

            ax.plot([xs[b] for b in LEVELS], d.retained.values, "-o", ms=4, color=cmap[fam](shade),
                    label=f"{fam} {MODELS[mo][2]:.1f}B")
            awq = s[(s.model == mo + "-awq") & (s.task == t)]
            if len(awq):
                ax.plot(xs[4] + 0.12, awq.retained.iloc[0], "*", ms=11, color=cmap[fam](shade), mec="k", mew=0.5)
        ax.axhline(0.85, ls="--", c="gray", lw=1)
        ax.axvspan(xs[8], xs[4], color="gray", alpha=0.06)
        ax.set_title(TNAME[t]); ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.25); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(LEVELS))); ax.set_xticklabels(["bf16" if b == 16 else f"{b}b" for b in LEVELS])
    axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("score / bf16 score"); axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("score / bf16 score")
    for ax in axes[1]:
        ax.set_xlabel("weight precision (RTN, group 128)")
    h, l = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(h, l, loc="lower center", ncol=8, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))
    fig.suptitle("Retained task performance vs weight precision (dashed: 85% threshold; ★: real AWQ-INT4 checkpoint)")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.04, 1, 1))
    fig.savefig(FIG / "fig1_retained_vs_bits.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def plot_heatmap(cl):
    piv = cl.pivot(index="model", columns="task", values="critical_bits").reindex(index=SWEEP, columns=TASKS)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 4.8))
    im = ax.imshow(piv.values, cmap="Reds", vmin=1, vmax=8)
    for i in range(piv.shape[0]):
        for j in range(piv.shape[1]):
            v = piv.values[i, j]

    return r


def cliffs(s):
    rows = []
    sw = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)]
    for (mo, t), d in sw.groupby(["model", "task"]):
        d = d.set_index("bits").retained.reindex(LEVELS)
        drops = {f"{hi}->{lo}": d[hi] - d[lo] for hi, lo in zip(LEVELS[:-1], LEVELS[1:])}
        crit = next((b for b in LEVELS if d[b] < 0.85), 1)
        big = max(drops, key=drops.get)
        rows.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, family=MODELS[mo][1], params_b=MODELS[mo][2], critical_bits=crit,
                         largest_drop_step=big, largest_drop=drops[big], drop_8_to_4=d[8] - d[4],
                         cliff_8_to_4=(d[8] - d[4]) > 0.15, ret8=d[8], ret6=d[6], ret5=d[5], ret4=d[4], ret3=d[3], ret2=d[2],
                         any_cliff_steps=",".join(k for k, v in drops.items() if v > 0.15)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def kl_analysis(s, cl):
    kls = [pd.read_csv(p) for p in sorted((RES / "kl").glob("*_g128.csv"))]
    if not kls:
        return None, {}
    kl = pd.concat(kls)
    wiki = kl[kl.task == "wikitext"][["model", "bits", "ppl"]].rename(columns={"ppl": "wiki_ppl"})
    w16 = wiki[wiki.bits == 16].set_index("model").wiki_ppl
    wiki["wiki_ppl_ratio"] = wiki.wiki_ppl / wiki.model.map(w16)
    m = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)].merge(kl[kl.task != "wikitext"], on=["model", "bits", "task"]) \
        .merge(wiki, on=["model", "bits"])
    m = m[m.bits != 16].copy()
    m["failed"] = m.retained < 0.85
    out = {"n_cells": len(m), "n_failed": int(m.failed.sum())}
    out["spearman_kl_retained"] = stats.spearmanr(m.kl, m.retained)._asdict()
    for col, sign in [("kl", 1), ("wiki_ppl_ratio", 1), ("top1_agree", -1)]:
        out[f"auc_{col}"] = roc_auc_score(m.failed, sign * m[col])
    # Optimal KL threshold (Youden J) with bootstrap CI.
    def youden(df):
        ths = np.unique(df.kl)
        best = max(ths, key=lambda th: ((df.kl >= th) & df.failed).sum() / max(1, df.failed.sum())
                   - ((df.kl >= th) & ~df.failed).sum() / max(1, (~df.failed).sum()))
        return best
    th = youden(m)
    bs = [youden(m.sample(len(m), replace=True, random_state=i)) for i in range(300)]
    out["youden_threshold"] = float(th); out["youden_ci"] = [float(np.percentile(bs, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(bs, 97.5))]
    for t0 in [0.3, th]:
        pred = m.kl >= t0
        out[f"at_{t0:.3f}"] = dict(sensitivity=float((pred & m.failed).sum() / max(1, m.failed.sum())),
                                   specificity=float((~pred & ~m.failed).sum() / max(1, (~m.failed).sum())))
    out["per_task_auc"] = {t: (roc_auc_score(d.failed, d.kl) if d.failed.nunique() == 2 else None)
                           for t, d in m.groupby("task")}
    out["kl_at_failure_by_task_median"] = m[m.failed].groupby("task").kl.median().to_dict()
    out["kl_at_healthy_by_task_median"] = m[~m.failed].groupby("task").kl.median().to_dict()
    # Lead-indicator test: for each (model, task) with a failure, KL at the last healthy level above it.
    lead = []
    for (mo, t), d in m.groupby(["model", "task"]):
        d = d.set_index("bits").reindex([b for b in LEVELS if b != 16])
        crit = next((b for b in d.index if d.loc[b, "failed"] is True or d.loc[b, "failed"] == 1), None)
        if crit is None:
            continue
        i = list(d.index).index(crit)
        prev = d.index[i - 1] if i > 0 else None
        lead.append(dict(model=mo, task=t, critical_bits=crit, kl_at_crit=d.loc[crit, "kl"],
                         prev_bits=prev, kl_prev=d.loc[prev, "kl"] if prev else np.nan,
                         ret_prev=d.loc[prev, "retained"] if prev else np.nan))
    lead = pd.DataFrame(lead)
    out["lead_n"] = len(lead)
    out["lead_frac_prev_kl_ge_0.3"] = float((lead.kl_prev >= 0.3).mean())
    out["lead_frac_crit_kl_ge_0.3"] = float((lead.kl_at_crit >= 0.3).mean())
    out["lead_median_kl_prev"] = float(lead.kl_prev.median()); out["lead_median_kl_crit"] = float(lead.kl_at_crit.median())
    lead.to_csv(RES / "kl_lead_analysis.csv", index=False)
    m.to_csv(RES / "kl_vs_accuracy.csv", index=False)
    return m, out


def plot_curves(s):
    sw = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 8.5), sharex=True, sharey=True)
    xs = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(LEVELS)}
    cmap = {"Qwen2.5": plt.cm.Blues, "Llama-3": plt.cm.Oranges, "Phi-3": plt.cm.Greens}
    for ax, t in zip(axes.flat, TASKS):
        for mo in SWEEP:
            d = sw[(sw.model == mo) & (sw.task == t)].set_index("bits").reindex(LEVELS)
            if d.retained.isna().all():
                continue
            fam = MODELS[mo][1]
            fam_models = [x for x in SWEEP if MODELS[x][1] == fam]
            shade = 0.45 + 0.5 * fam_models.index(mo) / max(1, len(fam_models) - 1)
            ax.plot([xs[b] for b in LEVELS], d.retained.values, "-o", ms=4, color=cmap[fam](shade),
                    label=f"{fam} {MODELS[mo][2]:.1f}B")
            awq = s[(s.model == mo + "-awq") & (s.task == t)]
            if len(awq):
                ax.plot(xs[4] + 0.12, awq.retained.iloc[0], "*", ms=11, color=cmap[fam](shade), mec="k", mew=0.5)
        ax.axhline(0.85, ls="--", c="gray", lw=1)
        ax.axvspan(xs[8], xs[4], color="gray", alpha=0.06)
        ax.set_title(TNAME[t]); ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.25); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(LEVELS))); ax.set_xticklabels(["bf16" if b == 16 else f"{b}b" for b in LEVELS])
    axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("score / bf16 score"); axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("score / bf16 score")
    for ax in axes[1]:
        ax.set_xlabel("weight precision (RTN, group 128)")
    h, l = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(h, l, loc="lower center", ncol=8, frameon=False, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))
    fig.suptitle("Retained task performance vs weight precision (dashed: 85% threshold; ★: real AWQ-INT4 checkpoint)")
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.04, 1, 1))
    fig.savefig(FIG / "fig1_retained_vs_bits.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def plot_heatmap(cl):
    piv = cl.pivot(index="model", columns="task", values="critical_bits").reindex(index=SWEEP, columns=TASKS)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 4.8))
    im = ax.imshow(piv.values, cmap="Reds", vmin=1, vmax=8)
    for i in range(piv.shape[0]):
        for j in range(piv.shape[1]):
            v = piv.values[i, j]
            ax.text(j, i, "none" if v == 1 else f"{int(v)}b", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9,
                    color="white" if v >= 5 else "black")
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(TASKS))); ax.set_xticklabels([TNAME[t].split(" (")[0] for t in TASKS], rotation=25, ha="right")
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(SWEEP))); ax.set_yticklabels([f"{MODELS[m][1]} {MODELS[m][2]:.1f}B" for m in SWEEP])
    ax.set_title("Critical precision: highest bit width with <85% of bf16 score")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="bits"); fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(FIG / "fig2_critical_bits_heatmap.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def plot_kl(m, out):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.8))
    ax = axes[0]
    mk = dict(zip(TASKS, "osD^vP"))
    for t in TASKS:
        d = m[m.task == t]
        ax.scatter(d.kl.clip(lower=1e-4), d.retained, s=18, marker=mk[t], label=TNAME[t].split(" (")[0], alpha=0.75)
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.axhline(0.85, ls="--", c="gray"); ax.axvline(0.3, ls=":", c="r", label="KL = 0.3 nats")
    ax.axvline(out["youden_threshold"], ls="-.", c="k", lw=1, label=f"best threshold {out['youden_threshold']:.2f}")
    ax.set_xlabel("task-specific KL(bf16 || quantized), nats/token"); ax.set_ylabel("retained score")
    ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.3); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.set_title("KL vs retained accuracy (all model×task×level)")
    ax = axes[1]
    sw = m.groupby(["bits", "task"]).kl.median().unstack().reindex([b for b in LEVELS if b != 16])
    for t in TASKS:
        if t in sw:
            ax.plot(range(len(sw)), sw[t], "-o", label=TNAME[t].split(" (")[0])
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(sw))); ax.set_xticklabels([f"{b}b" for b in sw.index]); ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.axhline(0.3, ls=":", c="r"); ax.set_ylabel("median KL across models (nats/token)"); ax.set_xlabel("weight precision")
    ax.set_title("KL grows ~4x per removed bit"); ax.legend(fontsize=7); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(FIG / "fig3_kl_vs_accuracy.png", dpi=150); plt.close(fig)


def main():
    df = load_items()
    s = summarize(df)
    s.to_csv(RES / "summary_scores.csv", index=False)
    tests = paired_tests(df); tests.to_csv(RES / "paired_tests.csv", index=False)
    cl = cliffs(s); cl.to_csv(RES / "cliffs.csv", index=False)
    plot_curves(s); plot_heatmap(cl)

    out = {}
    # H1/H2: task-level summary of retained fractions at 4 bits and 8->4 cliffs
    sw = s[(s.method == "rtn") & (s.group == 128)]
    out["retained_by_task_bits_median"] = sw.pivot_table(index="task", columns="bits", values="retained", aggfunc="median").round(3).to_dict()
    out["cliff_8_to_4_count_by_task"] = cl.groupby("task").cliff_8_to_4.sum().astype(int).to_dict()
    out["n_models"] = int(cl.model.nunique())
    out["critical_bits_median_by_task"] = cl.groupby("task").critical_bits.median().to_dict()
    # Task sensitivity ranking: mean retained at 4 and 3 bits (Friedman test across models)
    for b in (4, 3):
        piv = sw[sw.bits == b].pivot(index="model", columns="task", values="retained").dropna()
        out[f"friedman_retained_b{b}"] = dict(zip(["stat", "p"], map(float, stats.friedmanchisquare(*[piv[c] for c in piv]))))
        out[f"mean_retained_b{b}"] = piv.mean().round(3).to_dict()
    # H3: size vs critical bits (Spearman, all models and within Qwen family)
    out["spearman_size_critbits_all"] = stats.spearmanr(np.log(cl.params_b), cl.critical_bits)._asdict()
    q = cl[cl.family == "Qwen2.5"]
    out["spearman_size_critbits_qwen"] = stats.spearmanr(np.log(q.params_b), q.critical_bits)._asdict()
    out["critical_bits_by_model_mean"] = cl.groupby("model").critical_bits.mean().round(2).to_dict()
    # H4: KL
    m, kl_out = kl_analysis(s, cl)
    out["kl"] = kl_out
    if m is not None:
        plot_kl(m, kl_out)
    json.dump(out, open(RES / "hypothesis_tests.json", "w"), indent=1, default=float)
    print(json.dumps(out, indent=1, default=float))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

cd /data/summereunann/neurico-workspaces/quantization_failure_modes_20261020_001002_i9j0k1l2; cat > src/kl_queue.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: kl_queue.sh "GPU_LIST" NEED_GB -- model1 ...   (waits for bf16 generations + free GPU memory)
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."; source .venv/bin/activate
GPUS=$1; GB=$2; shift 3
need=$(python -c "print(int($GB*1024))")
for m in "$@"; do
  [ -f results/kl/${m}_g128.csv ] && continue
  until [ -f results/gens/${m}_b16_g128.jsonl ]; do sleep 30; done
  for try in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
    gpu=""
    while [ -z "$gpu" ]; do
      for g in $GPUS; do f=$(nvidia-smi -i $g --query-gpu=memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits); [ "$f" -gt "$need" ] && gpu=$g && break; done
      [ -z "$gpu" ] && sleep 30
    done
    echo "$(date) start on GPU $gpu" >> logs/kl_$m.log
    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$gpu python src/kl.py --model $m >> logs/kl_$m.log 2>&1 && break
    echo "$(date) fail $try" >> logs/kl_$m.log; sleep 30
  done
done
EOF
chmod +x src/kl_queue.sh

nohup src/kl_queue.sh "2 0 1 3" 20 -- qwen7b llama8b > /dev/null 2>&1 &
echo ok

content.text: Next, a multi-GPU serial queue for the larger models, with gens and KL interleaved per model:

input.command:
cd /data/summereunann/neurico-workspaces/quantization_failure_modes_20261020_001002_i9j0k1l2; cat > src/mq.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Serial multi-GPU queue. Each job: KIND MODEL NGPU GB_PER_GPU  (KIND = gen | kl)
# Waits until NGPU GPUs each have > GB_PER_GPU+0.6 GB free, then runs the job sharded over them.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."; source .venv/bin/activate
pick() {  # $1 = n gpus, $2 = MiB needed; prints comma list or nothing
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits | awk -F', ' -v need=$2 '$2>need{print $2, $1}' \
    | sort -rn | head -n $1 | awk '{print $2}' | paste -sd, | awk -F, -v n=$1 'NF==n'
}
while read kind m n gb; do
  [ -z "$kind" ] && continue
  if [ $kind = gen ]; then extra="--tp $n --gpu_gb $gb --eager --max_num_seqs 64 --batched_tokens 2048"; log=logs/gen_$m.log
  else [ -f results/kl/${m}_g128.csv ] && continue; extra="--max_gb_per_gpu $gb"; log=logs/kl_$m.log; fi
  need=$(python -c "print(int(($gb+0.6)*1024))")
  for try in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
    gpus=""; while [ -z "$gpus" ]; do gpus=$(pick $n $need); [ -z "$gpus" ] && sleep 20; done
    echo "$(date) $kind start on GPUs $gpus" >> $log
    if [ $kind = gen ]; then CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$gpus python src/generate.py --model $m $extra >> $log 2>&1 && break
    else CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$gpus python src/kl.py --model $m $extra >> $log 2>&1 && break; fi
    echo "$(date) $kind fail $try" >> $log; sleep 20
  done
  echo "$(date) $kind $m finished" >> logs/queue_status.txt
done < "$1"
EOF
chmod +x src/mq.sh
cat > logs/mq_jobs.txt << 'EOF'
gen qwen3b 2 4.2
kl qwen3b 2 4.0
gen qwen3b-awq 1 4.2
gen qwen7b 4 4.4
kl qwen7b 4 4.4
gen llama8b 4 4.4
kl llama8b 4 4.4
gen phi3mini 4 4.2
kl phi3mini 4 4.0
gen qwen7b-awq 2 4.4
gen qwen14b-awq 4 4.4
EOF
ps -eo pid,args | grep -E "[g]pu_queue.sh|[k]l_queue.sh|[g]enerate.py|[k]l.py" | cut -c1-140

content.text: While that waits, I'm writing an error-analysis script for the cliff-level failure taxonomy and correct↔wrong "flip" rates.

input.content:
"""Error taxonomy and answer flips for quantized models (RTN g128).

For each (model, task, bits) we count, among items that were correct (score>=0.5) in bf16:
  - lost: now wrong; split into
      degenerate: output hit max_tokens with low lexical diversity (distinct-2 < 0.5) or is empty
      truncated : hit max_tokens but not degenerate (rambling / over-long reasoning)
      wrong     : terminated normally but wrong answer (fluent error)
and among items wrong in bf16 how many became correct ("gained") — the noise floor of flips.
Writes results/error_taxonomy.csv and prints a compact table + example failures.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def main():
    df = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "results" / "item_scores.csv")
    df = df[(df.method == "rtn") & (df.group == 128) & (df.task != "creative")]
    base = df[df.bits == 16].set_index(["model", "task", "id"]).score
    rows = []
    for (mo, t, b), d in df[df.bits != 16].groupby(["model", "task", "bits"]):
        d = d.set_index("id")
        b0 = base.loc[(mo, t)].reindex(d.index)
        was = b0 >= 0.5

pick() {  # $1 = n gpus, $2 = MiB needed; prints comma list or nothing

  [ $kind = kl ] && [ -f results/kl/${m}_g128.csv ] && continue

content.text: Memory moved under me again. I'll wrap the judge in the same wait-for-free-slices logic:

input.command:
cd /data/summereunann/neurico-workspaces/quantization_failure_modes_20261020_001002_i9j0k1l2; cat > src/judge_loop.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Run src/judge.py when a config fits: 1 GPU x 7.5 GB or 2 GPUs x 4.4 GB (TP). Retries up to 12 times.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."; source .venv/bin/activate
pick() { nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits | awk -F', ' -v need=$2 '$2>need{print $2, $1}' \
    | sort -rn | head -n $1 | awk '{print $2}' | paste -sd, | awk -F, -v n=$1 'NF==n'; }
for try in $(seq 1 12); do
  gpus=""
  while [ -z "$gpus" ]; do
    for c in 1:7.5 2:4.4; do n=${c%%:*}; gb=${c##*:}; gpus=$(pick $n $(python -c "print(int(($gb+0.5)*1024))")); [ -n "$gpus" ] && break; done
    [ -z "$gpus" ] && sleep 15
  done
  echo "$(date) judge start on $gpus" >> logs/judge.log
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$gpus python src/judge.py --gpu_gb $gb --tp $n >> logs/judge.log 2>&1 && break
  echo "$(date) judge fail $try" >> logs/judge.log; sleep 15
done
EOF
chmod +x src/judge_loop.sh; nohup src/judge_loop.sh > /dev/null 2>&1 & echo ok
